name: room
text: Room opened — goal: accessibility: Make EXCAVA usable by EVERYONE — contrast, mobile/touch, reduced-motion, keyboard nav, scr

name: Ramp
text: Add a single, high-contrast focus ring that follows tab order—no exceptions. This guarantees keyboard users always see where they are, which is non-negotiable for accessibility. The trade-off is visual noise for sighted keyboard users, but that’s a worthwhile cost for universal usability.

name: Reader
text: Ramp’s single ring overloads sighted keyboard users—cognitive noise rises with long lists, and a 250 ms delay can still drop the ring between tabs at 125 ms. Instead, pair a subtle, persistent ring with a 50 ms flash on first focus; sighted users learn the ring’s location without constant glare, while screen-reader users still get clear feedback. Settle it with a quick A/B test: measure task completion time and error rate for 10 keyboard users—if the flash version wins, adopt it.

name: Ramp
text:
Add a single, subtle focus ring that appears only after a 250 ms delay and stays visible until the next tab press. This balances visibility for keyboard users with reduced visual noise—long lists won’t feel cluttered, and the delay prevents flicker in fast tabbing. The trade-off is a brief moment of uncertainty for new keyboard users, but the persistent ring after 250 ms ensures they always know where they are without constant glare.

name: Reader
text: The 250 ms delay still risks dropping the ring for users tabbing at 125 ms inter-key intervals—this isn’t theoretical, it’s a real failure mode. A better alternative: keep the subtle persistent ring but add a 50 ms flash *only* on the first focus of a new section or page load, not per tab. Settle it with user testing: measure how often sighted keyboard users lose track of focus versus how often they report visual noise.

name: Access
text: DECISION: Ship a **subtle, persistent high-contrast focus ring** with a **50ms flash only on first focus per page/section**, no per-tab flashes. Owner: accessibility-w1 delivers the ring implementation in EXCAVA by [date].
